**Idea 1: an edit only matters if its node is connected.** An edge out of node 1 or node 2 only helps if that node receives a signal. For example, if edge 0 is `none`, node 1 is all zeros, so adding a convolution on edge 4 does almost nothing.

**Idea 2: removing an edge hurts more when the output has fewer other inputs.** Node 3 receives edges 3, 4 and 5. Deleting one of them costs more when another is already missing, because the output may lose its last good path or its residual-style shortcut. For the same reason, adding `skip_connect` or `nor_conv_3x3` gains more when it fills an empty edge than when it replaces another operation.
